[RAZI-FULL:v15p86#2/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · المتكلمون | reports | The theologians argue that the command to remember God within oneself establishes inward speech, which they identify as inner remembrance.

[RAZI-FULL:v15p86#2/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Calling God 'your Lord' here, rather than using another divine name, signals care, nearness, favor, and beneficence, and should make the servant rejoice.

[RAZI-FULL:v15p86/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Verbal remembrance without awareness in the heart is fruitless, just as uttering 'I sold' or 'I bought' without understanding those words does not effect a sale.
[RAZI-FULL:v15p86/r5] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | Rāzī recounts a spiritual master's method: after forty days of retreat and purification, the disciple hears the ninety-nine names and identifies which most moves the heart; steady repetition of that name may open disclosures.

[RAZI-FULL:v15p88#2/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Morning turns people from sleep like death to waking like life and the world from darkness to light; evening reverses the change. These striking transitions display God's wisdom and boundless power, warranting remembrance at both times.
